subject: Civil Engineering
title: Stone Arch Bridges: Ancient Innovation
description: A 60-second lesson on Stone Arch Bridges: Ancient Innovation.

hook.text: The Pont du Gard in France has carried water and traffic for 2,000 years.

buildup.text: Stone arches convert all loads into compression — stone's strongest mode.

discovery.text: Centering — a temporary wood frame — supports the arch until the keystone locks in.

twist.text: Once the keystone is placed, the centering is removed and the arch holds itself.

climax.text: Some Roman arches survived because the mortar hardened stronger than the stones.

punchline.text: An arch holds itself up by trying to fall apart.

quiz.question: What is 'centering' in arch bridge construction?
options: The process of finding the exact middle of the span
A temporary frame that supports the arch until the keystone is placed
A technique for balancing loads on each side of the bridge
